content.title: About
content.content: The chocolate ice cream bar (item 440) is a frozen dessert made from creamy ice cream coated with a thin layer of milk chocolate. It combines a smooth ice‑cream texture with a crunchy chocolate shell, making it a popular treat year‑round.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first chocolate ice‑cream bar was introduced in the United States in the 1920s.
The chocolate coating protects the ice cream from melting, allowing the bar to stay solid at slightly higher temperatures.
Emulsifiers and stabilizers are often added to keep the cream smooth after freezing.
Variants around the world may include nuts, caramel, or fruit pieces.
Bars are usually sold in individual wrappers, which makes them easy to transport and vending‑machine friendly.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Dairy ice cream provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Milk ingredients supply vitamins B2 and B12, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates and fats offers a fast source of energy.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Chocolate stimulates serotonin production, which can lift mood.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Ice cream contains a notable amount of water, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Bars often contain a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Dairy components may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Nut and soy allergies
items.content: Some recipes use nuts or soy lecithin, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Melting if stored improperly
items.content: Storing above –12 °C can cause the chocolate shell to crack and the ice cream to melt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the bar slowly, allowing the chocolate coating to soften slightly while the ice cream releases its flavor. It’s convenient for on‑the‑go snacking, post‑workout treats, or as a dessert after a meal.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen at –18 °C or lower. Once removed from the wrapper, consume within 30 minutes to prevent melting. Do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
